origins.why: storage crop, dominant North American fresh supply
culls and peelers, not extra-fancy fresh

channels.label: Grower-shipper FOB
channels.use: Buy a packed carton at Yakima / Wenatchee / Simcoe. Best when you can take a truckload.

channels.label: Licensed importer
channels.use: Chilean / NZ fruit. They already paid duty, inspection, and ripening risk.

channels.label: Ontario / US terminal
channels.use: Broken pallets, mixed sizes. Pay wholesale ask; good for first loads.

channels.label: Processor / packer culls
channels.use: If you make juice, sauce, slices. Farm processing price is far below extra-fancy FOB.

channels.label: Season program
channels.use: Float off USDA shipping-point + margin. Fair when you need weekly volume.

origins.why: foodservice rounds; not the same SKU as vine-ripe
processed $/ton is a different market than fresh

channels.label: Ontario greenhouse direct
channels.use: Cluster / TOV. Pay greenhouse FOB, skip long haul.

channels.label: Mexico crossing importer
channels.use: Winter volume. Check Nogales / McAllen FOB + freight + CFIA.

channels.label: Florida shipper
channels.use: Mature-green for foodservice, not grocery vine-ripe.

channels.label: Terminal / DC
channels.use: Spot shorts. Compare to AAFC wholesale mid.

channels.label: Paste / dice plant
channels.use: Only if you buy processed. NASS processing series, not fresh.

origins.why: processing cwt is not a clamshell

channels.label: Local farm / auction
channels.use: June peak only. Quality clock is 48 hours.

channels.label: CA / FL / MX FOB
channels.use: Driscoll-style or independent shipper. Freight and shrink dominate.

channels.label: Winter importer
channels.use: Mexico / Florida through a licensed desk.

channels.label: IQF / puree
channels.use: If you process. Do not use fresh FOB as the bench.

origins.why: new crop before storage is gone

channels.label: Shed FOB
channels.use: 50-lb or tote. Most honest print.

channels.label: Potato broker
channels.use: Mix sizes and storage lots.

channels.label: Fry plant contract
channels.use: Different variety and solids spec.

origins.why: you buy a bag, not a head

channels.label: Salinas / Yuma FOB
channels.use: Carton 24s. Watch freight — lettuce is mostly water.

channels.label: Fresh-cut plant
channels.use: If you need kits. Price is processing + film + labor, not farm cwt.

channels.label: Terminal
channels.use: Emergency shorts only.

channels.label: Shed FOB
channels.use: 50-lb sacks. Compare NASS cwt to AAFC Vancouver/Toronto ask.

channels.label: CA / MX FOB
channels.use: Crown carton. Freight + ice matter.

channels.label: Frozen floret
channels.use: If you process or foodservice. Do not bench against fresh crowns.

origins.why: juice and dice pay a different number

channels.label: Cello FOB
channels.use: Retail packs.

channels.label: Jumbo / juice
channels.use: If you process. Ask for jumbo, not cello.

channels.label: Ontario GH
channels.use: English seedless. Not comparable to field slicers.

channels.label: Mexico importer
channels.use: Winter field.

channels.label: CA FOB lug
channels.use: Packed table fruit.

channels.label: Chile / Peru importer
channels.use: Winter. Duty and arrival quality are the risk.

channelsGeneric.name: Port / crossing
channelsGeneric.data: Census unit value + AMS import FOB

fairnessRules.farm: A farm-gate quote should sit near this month's NASS percentile, same utilization (fresh vs process).
fairnessRules.fob: Packed FOB is farm + pack/cool. Expect 15–40% over farm-gate on fresh cartons.
fairnessRules.landed: Landed Toronto ≈ FOB + freight + duty/broker. If a 'FOB' quote already exceeds destination wholesale, walk away or check quality.
fairnessRules.wholesale: AAFC mid is an asking range to retail, not a cleared trade.
fairnessRules.process: Never bench processed $/ton against fresh extra-fancy.
